title: Surgical outcome of Descemet’s stripping automated endothelial keratoplasty for bullous keratopathy secondary to argon laser iridotomy

groups.description: DSAEK for bullous keratopathy secondary to argon laser iridotomy (ALI group); 47 eyes Descemet-stripping DSAEK and 7 eyes non-Descemet-stripping DSAEK (nDSAEK) (Table 2). Simultaneous phacoemulsification with IOL implantation before DSAEK in the same operation in 37 of the 54 eyes (combined left null: only part of the group).

DSAEK for pseudophakic bullous keratopathy (PBK group); 24 eyes DSAEK and 4 eyes nDSAEK (Table 2). Every eye pseudophakic, so no same-session cataract surgery (none reported; simultaneous cataract surgery stated only for the ALI and FED groups).

DSAEK for Fuchs endothelial dystrophy (FED group); all 21 eyes Descemet-stripping DSAEK (Table 2). Simultaneous cataract surgery in the same operation in 13 of the 21 eyes (combined left null: only part of the group).

notes: Retrospective review of the medical records of all consecutive patients who underwent DSAEK for ALI-BK, FED or PBK between April 2007 and December 2010; the authors list their exclusions with counts, all preoperative (suspected combined ALI and FED causes, previous penetrating keratoplasty, macular dysfunction after retinal detachment, Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome, end-stage glaucoma, bullous keratopathy from birth injury). The Results statement that every eye was followed for at least 6 months describes the observed follow-up; it is not an inclusion criterion, and no operated eye was left out for lack of follow-up.

Graft clarity at 6 months, graft rejection and complications are reported (Tables 4, 6); no eye underwent re-keratoplasty within 6 months; how eyes without a clear graft enter the means is not stated.
Spherical equivalent, induced astigmatism and keratometry (Table 4) and endothelial cell density (Table 5) are tabulated: notes only. Table 1 (demographics) is an image and is not used.
